message.content:
Build VISITOR ANALYTICS with a live activity GLOBE for the Nxeon admin portal at /opt/nxeon. Other agents edit OTHER areas concurrently — touch ONLY YOUR OWNED FILES.

## PRIMER
Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma. `"use server"` = async-only. `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`; admin gate `import { requireArea } from "@/lib/rbac"` → `await requireArea("analytics")`. Design: `.card`,`.table-shell`,`.btn-*`; `import { PageHeader, Badge, timeAgo } from "@/components/ui/primitives"`; charts in `@/components/ui/charts`. NEW models: `Visit{ip,path,referrer,ua,kind("marketing"|"portal"),userId,country,region,city,lat,lng,geocoded,createdAt}`, `GeoCache{ip(@id),country,region,city,lat,lng}`.

## TASK
1. **Capture** page views. `components/VisitTracker.tsx` (`"use client"`, default export, tiny/invisible): on mount, POST `{ path, referrer }` to `/api/track` (fire-and-forget, dedupe rapid repeats per path via sessionStorage). `app/api/track/route.ts`: reads client IP from `x-forwarded-for`, records a `Visit` (kind from a `?k=` param or default "marketing"), skips bots by UA, never throws. (Orchestrator mounts `<VisitTracker/>` in the marketing layout and portal Shell.)
2. **Geo-enrich** (best-effort, no key). `worker/geo.ts` exports `geoEnrichSweep()`: find recent `Visit`s with `geocoded=false`, look up each IP — first from `GeoCache`, else call the free `http://ip-api.com/json/<ip>?fields=status,country,regionName,city,lat,lon` (rate-limit to ≤40/min, skip private IPs), upsert `GeoCache`, copy country/region/city/lat/lng onto the Visit + set `geocoded=true`. Robust to failures. (Orchestrator calls this from the worker loop.)
3. **Admin page** `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` (`requireArea("analytics")`): live visitors (distinct IPs in last 5 min), today's views, top referrers, top countries/cities, a recent-visits table (time/IP/geo/path/referrer/marketing-vs-portal), and the globe.
4. **Globe** `components/admin/VisitorGlobe.tsx` (`"use client"`): a self-contained rotating 3D-looking globe (WebGL via raw canvas/`<canvas>` OR a canvas-2D orthographic globe — **no external libraries, no three.js**) that plots recent geocoded visits as glowing dots at their lat/lng with subtle pulse/arc animation; auto-rotate; respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keep it performant (≤ a few hundred points). `components/admin/VisitorStats.tsx` for the stat cards/tables.
5. `lib/analytics.ts` — plain helpers (aggregations: liveVisitors, topReferrers, topCountries, recentVisits).

## OWNED FILES (create ONLY these)
`app/api/track/route.ts`, `components/VisitTracker.tsx`, `worker/geo.ts`, `lib/analytics.ts`, `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx`, `components/admin/VisitorGlobe.tsx`, `components/admin/VisitorStats.tsx`.

## HARD RULES
Never touch layouts/Shell/schema/next.config/worker-index/rbac/db/auth/ROADMAP/docs/sitemap or others' files. No build/prisma/generate/restart/commit. No new deps. `"use server"` = async-only. Client IP only from `x-forwarded-for` (nginx sets it).

## REPORT
Files created; how capture + geo + globe work; INTEGRATION NEEDED (mount `<VisitTracker/>` in marketing layout + Shell; call `geoEnrichSweep()` in the worker loop; nav link `/admin/visitors` in the analytics area); risks.

1	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
47	  "/admin/users": "clients",
48	  "/admin/support": "support",
49	  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
50	  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
51	  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
52	  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
53	  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
54	  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
55	  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
56	  "/admin/billing": "billing",
57	  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
58	  "/admin/plans": "billing",
59	  "/admin/coupons": "billing",
60	  "/admin/game-plans": "billing",
61	  "/admin/feedback": "support",
62	  "/admin/logs": "platform",
63	  "/admin/domains": "platform",
64	  "/admin/grant": "platform",
65	  "/admin/audit": "platform",
66	  "/admin/automation": "platform",
67	  "/admin/settings": "platform",
68	  "/admin/staff": "platform",
69	  "/admin/email-templates": "platform",
70	  "/admin/games": "platform",
71	  "/admin/blog": "platform",
72	};
73	
74	export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
75	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
76	}
77	
78	export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
79	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
84	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
85	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
86	 */
87	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
88	  const user = await realUser();
89	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
90	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
91	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
92	  return user;
93	}

The Prisma client already exposes both delegates. All seven files are created and typecheck clean.

## Summary

Built the visitor analytics feature for the Nxeon admin portal. All work confined to the seven owned files; no shared files touched.

### Files created
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/analytics.ts` — read-only aggregation helpers: `liveVisitors`, `todayViews`, `viewsInWindow`, `uniqueVisitors`, `topReferrers`, `topCountries`, `topCities`, `recentVisits`, `globePoints`, plus a `referrerHost` normalizer. All scoped to short windows with capped `take`.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/api/track/route.ts` — POST capture endpoint (`runtime="nodejs"`). Reads client IP from `x-forwarded-for` first hop only, kind from `?k=` (portal|marketing, default marketing), drops bots/empty UAs via a coarse regex, strips same-origin referrers, and is wrapped so it never throws.
- `/opt/nxeon/components/VisitTracker.tsx` — `"use client"` default export, renders `null`. Fires a fire-and-forget `keepalive` POST on each `usePathname` change; dedupes repeats of the same path per tab via sessionStorage (30s window). Accepts `kind` prop.
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/geo.ts` — exports `geoEnrichSweep()`. Loads up to 200 pending (`geocoded=false`) visits, skips private/loopback/link-local IPs, checks `GeoCache` first, else calls the keyless `ip-api.com` endpoint (capped at 40 external lookups/sweep, paced 1.5s apart, 6s timeout). Upserts `GeoCache`, copies country/region/city/lat/lng onto the visit, sets `geocoded=true`. Shares one lookup across same-IP bursts; every op is defensive.
- `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/VisitorGlobe.tsx` — `"use client"` canvas-2D orthographic globe, zero dependencies. Shaded sphere + graticule, auto-rotation, front-hemisphere-only glowing pulsing dots (emerald=marketing, purple=portal), limb fade. Honors `prefers-reduced-motion` (static frame), HiDPI-scaled, capped at the ~300 points passed in.
- `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/VisitorStats.tsx` — `RankedList` (count-bar lists) and `RecentVisitsTable` (time/IP/geo/path/referrer/source badge), using `.card`/`.table-shell`/`Badge`/`timeAgo`.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` — `requireArea("analytics")`, `force-dynamic`. Stat cards (live 5-min, today, 7d views, 7d uniques), globe + top countries/cities, top referrers + recent-visits table.

### How it works
Capture: `<VisitTracker/>` beacons each route change to `/api/track`, which records a `Visit`. Enrich: the worker periodically runs `geoEnrichSweep()` to attach locations. Display: the admin page reads aggregates and feeds recent geocoded coordinates to the globe.

### INTEGRATION NEEDED (orchestrator — not my files)
- Mount `<VisitTracker />` in the marketing layout (default kind) and `<VisitTracker kind="portal" />` in `components/portal/Shell.tsx`.
- Call `geoEnrichSweep()` from the worker loop in `worker/index.ts` (import from `./geo`) on a timer, e.g. every ~1–2 min — mirror the existing `lastSweep` pattern.
- Add an `/admin/visitors` nav link under the analytics area, and add `"/admin/visitors": "analytics"` to `HREF_AREA` in `lib/rbac.ts` so the route gates correctly (currently defaults to platform/ADMIN-only, which still works but the mapping is cleaner).

### Risks
- `ip-api.com` is HTTP-only and free-tier rate-limited; the 40/sweep cap plus pacing keeps it under 45/min, but a large backlog drains slowly across sweeps (by design).
- Under a real reverse proxy chain, `x-forwarded-for[0]` is the client only if nginx is trusted to set it (the primer confirms it does).
- Prisma client already exposes `visit`/`geoCache` delegates, so no generate is required; verified in `node_modules/.prisma/client`.
- Bot filtering is heuristic UA matching — some bots with browser-like UAs may slip through.
